findings.title: All app modules are still imported eagerly when this module loads
findings.body: Every `import("./x")` here is evaluated as soon as `@calcom/app-store` is first imported, so all 28 app packages still get loaded on every import. The PR is meant to load them lazily, and this layout only turns the values into promises. Using thunks (`applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) and calling `await appStore[key]?.()` at the call sites would load only the app that is needed. As written, a failed import of an app nobody asked for also becomes an unhandled rejection when the module loads.

findings.title: The try/catch no longer catches errors from getCalendar
findings.body: Before, `getCalendar` ran synchronously inside `forEach`, so an exception (for example a CalendarService constructor throwing) reached the surrounding `try/catch` and was logged. Now the callback is `async`, so that exception becomes a rejected promise that nobody awaits. It skips the catch on line 135 and surfaces as an unhandled rejection. Using `for...of` with `await`, or `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))`, would keep the error handling. The same pattern is in packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:125 and packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:553 (that one has no try/catch at all).

contracts.action: getCalendarCredentials now returns `calendar` as a Promise
contracts.before_after: Every caller (viewer.tsx:340, viewer.tsx:415, apps/web/pages/api/availability/calendar.ts:83) only passes the result to getConnectedCalendars, which awaits `item.calendar` inside its try block
contracts.failure_mode: A rejected getCalendar is caught by the try/catch in getConnectedCalendars and shown as an error entry

contracts.action: Reschedule-request cancels calendar events inside forEach(async)
contracts.equivalent_path: handleCancelBooking awaits getCalendar in a for loop and collects the promises
contracts.before_after: Before, deleteEvent promises were dropped as well. Now getCalendar errors also escape the caller
contracts.visible_effect: No visible change. The deletions run fire-and-forget

summary: This PR changes the app store so each app package is loaded with `import()`. It also makes `getCalendar` and `getVideoAdapters` async and updates their callers. I found no type or flow breakage: every caller of `getCalendarCredentials` goes through `getConnectedCalendars`, which awaits the calendar inside its try block. Two non-blocking points. First, the object of `import()` calls in index.ts still loads every app when the module loads, so nothing is actually lazy. Second, three reschedule paths now use `forEach(async ...)`, so errors from `getCalendar` skip the try/catch and become unhandled rejections.
